sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Livonia?
sections.html:
The City of Livonia assesses and bills its own property tax, and Wayne County steps in only after a bill goes delinquent. The Assessment Department sets values and handles exemption forms. The Treasurer's Office, on the first floor of City Hall at 33000 Civic Center Drive, mails real and personal property tax bills on July 1 and December 1 and collects the payments.

Those payments are split among several taxing bodies: the City of Livonia, Livonia Public Schools, Clarenceville Public Schools, Schoolcraft College, the State of Michigan education tax, Wayne County, Wayne County RESA and Oakland ISD. A house in the northeast corner of the city that falls in the Clarenceville district carries a different mix of levies than one in the Livonia Public Schools territory.

  • Treasurer, bills, due dates, deferrals, special assessments, millage questions: (734) 466-2245.
  • Assessment Department, valuation and exemption forms: (734) 466-2220.
  • Water account: (734) 466-2278.
  • Inspection, for outstanding permits, violations, vacant or abandoned property registration fees and certificate of occupancy: (734) 466-2580.

Summer taxes are billed July 1 and due September 14. Winter taxes are billed December 1 and due February 14. When a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day. Checks go to City of Livonia, Treasurer, 33000 Civic Center Drive, Livonia, MI 48154.

Livonia tax bill calendar and city fees

Printouts or screenshots from the city's online system do not count as an original tax bill. A title company closing a Livonia sale should bring the original, or the $5 fee applies. Delinquent personal property tax stays with the city treasurer, while delinquent real property tax moves to the county.

sections.h2: Looking up a tax bill and special assessments
sections.html:
The city runs an online property inquiry system at livoniatax.org, using BS&A software. Agree to the disclaimer, search by address, and enter only the street name without Road, Street or Avenue, or just the house number. Click the property, open the Tax Information tab, and the taxes appear by year and season, with a detailed breakdown behind each year.

Errors on the site do not cancel taxes or special assessments owed. The official records at City Hall cover current-year collections only, and payments on delinquent taxes do not appear online. To check a delinquent balance, contact the Wayne County Treasurer.

Special assessments are a separate item. Email specials@livonia.gov to request the status on a parcel. Vacant and abandoned property fees, permit issues and violations are missing from the online system, so a seller who wants a clean closing should ask Inspection for those directly.

An affidavit for the principal residence exemption filed on or before June 1 earns the exemption on that year's summer and winter levy and later years while the home remains the owner's principal residence. One filed after June 1 and on or before November 1 applies to the current winter levy and later levies.

The city also publishes a form letting a homeowner defer the due date of winter taxes on a principal residence without penalty or interest, for a stated period set each year. Ask the Treasurer's Office which year's form and deadline applies. Hardship exemptions run through the local assessing unit, so Livonia owners in a tight spot should start with the Assessment Department, not the county.

Religious, charitable and educational exemption forms, plus personal property forms, are on the Assessment Department page, which accepts forms by email, mail or the City Hall drop box on the east side of the building.

sections.h2: If Livonia property taxes go unpaid
sections.html:
Unpaid summer and winter bills are forwarded to the Wayne County Treasurer. On March 1 unpaid taxes become delinquent at the county, adding a 4 percent administration fee and 1 percent interest per month. A $15 collection fee follows on October 1. The next March 1 the parcel forfeits to the county treasurer, with a $175 fee and recording fees, and interest rises to 1.5 percent per month retroactive to the first delinquency.

Foreclosure follows. Michigan's three-year process ends with the circuit court entering a judgment, and unpaid taxes on March 31 of the third year mean the owner loses the property. Wayne County sends at least ten notices before that point.

Owners with a financial hardship can apply for a Wayne County payment plan. The income limit is 125 percent of the federal level, and the application needs photo ID, a copy of the deed, proof of occupancy and proof of income. After a foreclosure, the former owner can claim remaining auction proceeds by filing a notice of intent by July 1 of that year.

Livonia is a Wayne County city of about 95,500 people at the 2020 census, with more than 40,000 housing units and only 2.7 percent of them vacant. Many homes here have been owned for decades, so a long-held house often has a taxable value well below its market value, a gap that closes for the next owner after a sale.

Most Livonia homes sold with tax due close like any other. The title company gets a payoff, pays the city or county from the seller's proceeds, and records the deed. Work through it in this order:

  • Pull the current bill at livoniatax.org and note the season and amount.
  • Ask the Treasurer's Office at (734) 466-2245 whether the bill is still with the city.
  • If the bill is delinquent, ask Wayne County for the payoff figure, since City Hall no longer holds the balance.
  • Email specials@livonia.gov for special assessments and call Inspection at (734) 466-2580 for open permits or violations.

Owners behind on taxes, with an inherited house or a place that needs work, can ask for a cash offer and have the payoff settled at the table.

faqs.q: When is the Livonia summer tax due?
faqs.a: September 14. The summer bill is mailed July 1, and if September 14 lands on a weekend or holiday the due date becomes the next business day.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Livonia winter taxes?
faqs.a: Mail a check payable to the City of Livonia to Treasurer, 33000 Civic Center Drive, Livonia, MI 48154, or use the Treasurer's Office on the first floor of City Hall. Winter bills are due February 14.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a delinquent Livonia tax bill?
faqs.a: The Wayne County Treasurer. Delinquent real property taxes are turned over to the county, and the city's own records show current-year collections only.

faqs.q: How do I get the principal residence exemption in Livonia?
faqs.a: File the affidavit with the Assessment Department. Filing by June 1 covers that year's summer and winter taxes, and filing after June 1 through November 1 covers the winter levy.

faqs.q: Which school districts tax Livonia homes?
faqs.a: Livonia Public Schools serves most of the city, and a portion of the northeast is in Clarenceville Public Schools. Both appear among the bodies that receive the city's collections.
